native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: BA-degree completion is lowest for Black respondents relative to White respondents, and the -0.9568 figure is that Black-vs-White contrast: the log odds ratio for Black relative to White (White is the reference), corresponding to an odds ratio of exp(-0.9568) = 0.384, i.e. Black respondents' odds of completing a BA are about 38% of White respondents'. On this file the unadjusted Black-vs-White log OR is -1.005703 (OR 0.3658, 95% CI -1.406 to -0.606) and a mildly SES-adjusted model gives about -0.941 (OR 0.390), so -0.9568 lies on the Black-vs-White adjustment path; it is the only pair whose standard-model range contains the value (9/79 specifications reach it, versus 0/79 for Hispanic-vs-White and 0/79 for Black-vs-Hispanic). Hispanic-vs-White (crude -0.924136, OR 0.3969) is the runner-up and cannot be formally excluded, while Black-vs-Hispanic (crude -0.0816) is decisively excluded.
native_result.WorkflowB: Cleaned data/nls_ses_processed.csv (dropped undocumented 'Unnamed: 0' index column, recoded BA DEGREE COMPLETED True/False to 1/0; verified 0 missing values, 0 duplicate CASE IDs, 3 clean race labels, no sentinel codes). Then ran a 14-family specification search producing 1,404 distinct race-contrast statistics: unadjusted 2x2 tables in all 6 ordered directions; race-only logistic under all three reference codings plus no-intercept and two-race-subsample equivalents; race plus all 32 subsets of {SES, ABILITY, PERCENTILE, FAMSIZE, SEX} fitted with GLM/IRLS/hand-rolled Logit; probit and cloglog links; Firth penalised logistic; one-race-vs-pooled-others; Mantel-Haenszel ORs stratified by each covariate; within-sex and within-SES-quartile fits; race x covariate interaction models (main effect = contrast at covariate mean); coarsened covariate encodings (dichotomised, tertile, quartile, log) to generate partial adjustment; and outlier-trimmed samples. Each statistic was scored against -0.9568, then diagnosed for (i) attainability within the standard no-interaction range per pair, (ii) direction of travel under adjustment (attenuation vs amplification), (iii) bootstrap sampling uncertainty, and (iv) a random-target calibration quantifying how close the best of 1,404 specs gets by chance. Conclusion drawn from attainability plus adjustment direction rather than digit matching.
